title: Capstone: North gross margin
prompt: In B7, work out the North gross margin as a percentage, rounded to 1 decimal, and wrap it in IFERROR so an empty region shows a blank instead of an error.

require.message: The capstone has to survive a missing region: wrap the calculation in IFERROR.
The capstone totals by region: build the revenue with SUMIF.
The capstone reports margin to one decimal: use ROUND.

hints.func-iferror: Wrap the whole calculation in IFERROR(value, "") so a region with no revenue shows a blank instead of #DIV/0!.
hints.func-sumif: Total the North revenue and the North cost separately — SUM would mix in every region.
hints.func-round: The margin needs ROUND to 1 decimal; without it the cell shows a long string of digits.
hints.one-decimal: ROUND's second argument is the number of decimals, and this answer wants 1.
hints.require-ref: Match on the region column and add the revenue column, so the answer follows the table.
hints.value: Work in stages: North revenue, minus North cost, over North revenue, times 100. That is (2500 − 1380) / 2500 × 100 = 44.8.
hints.error: An error escaping this cell means the division ran before IFERROR could catch it, or IFERROR has no second argument — so there is nothing to show when a region comes back empty. IFERROR(value, "") goes on the outside, around everything.

docs.explain: This is the whole track in one cell. SUMIF picks the North rows out of both money columns: revenue 1500 + 1000 = 2500, cost 800 + 580 = 1380. Gross margin is (revenue − cost) / revenue, so (2500 − 1380) / 2500 = 0.448, and multiplying by 100 gives 44.8 percent. ROUND with 1 decimal keeps it there. IFERROR is the professional finish: if a region ever has no revenue the division would raise #DIV/0!, and wrapping the result in IFERROR(...,"") turns that loud error into a quiet blank that a chart can still read. Notice the order — ROUND sits inside IFERROR, so the error check sees the finished number, and the empty string is a text value, which is why the cell has to be formatted as text-friendly or left alone rather than forced to a number format.

errors.text: The revenue lookup found nothing, so the division is by zero. IFERROR is what hides it.
Quotes around the region name are missing, so North is read as a name that Excel does not know.
Multiplying by 100 twice, or forgetting that ROUND on 0.448 with 1 decimal gives 0.4 — check which side of the percent you are on.

docs.atWork: This is the monthly-region-summary cell. SUMIF for the numerator and denominator, ROUND to keep the finance team happy, IFERROR so a new region with no sales yet does not paint a red error across the dashboard.
docs.outcome: The whole track in one cell: margin, rounded, error-proof.
docs.teaches: SUMIF, ROUND and IFERROR nested in one formula
